messages:
maya: Heads-up — we saw a regional surge in tok-bucket drop rates for org keys in eu-west yesterday evening. Queue length hit 90% for a few GPU pools.
jon: Saw that. Is it more traffic or slow drains from long-context jobs?
aisha: Mostly long-context Llama jobs + a bad networking flake that delayed KV cache warmups in eu-west-2. Head latency spiked which killed throughput.
nikhil: Can we avoid dropping tokens blindly? Customers hit 429s even when a couple GPUs were idle due to imbalanced routing.
maya: Proposal: move from fixed token-bucket refill to capacity-aware refill. Refill rate = base_rate * (available_capacity / total_capacity). That gives organic backpressure.
jon: I like capacity-aware refill. Also allow short burst cap = min(bucket_size, free_slots * burst_multiplier).
aisha: Needs to be per-region and per-pool. Global keys currently get routed across regions and we lost locality.
nikhil: +1 on region scoping. We should fall back to a compatible model in another region only if the target region is saturated AND latency delta < 30ms.
maya: Another detail: soft vs hard quotas. Soft = token-bucket enforcement that drops when queue > soft_threshold. Hard = absolute per-org limit that denies immediately when exceeded. Soft should be coupled to real-time queue metrics.
jon: We also need leaky-bucket variant for long-running streaming calls where tokens accrue slower but sustained. Token-bucket handles bursts; leaky handles steady drains. Mix both?
aisha: Implement hybrid: token-bucket for request admission, leaky-window for sustained bandwidth per minute. If leaky-window exceeded, degrade to background queue with priority=low.
nikhil: Telemetry to add: per-key token refill rate, per-pool available_gpus, queue_depth, avg_head_latency, drop_reason tag (saturated|timeout|network).
sre-bot: alert: eu-west-2 gpu-pool-3 queue_depth >= 85% (2026-02-18T20:12:03Z)
maya: Example config sketch:
```
rate_limits:
  org_default:
    base_rate: 100 rps
    bucket_size: 200
    burst_multiplier: 2
    soft_threshold: 0.7 # fraction of pool queue
    hard_limit: 1000 rps
  capacity_aware: true
  region_scope: true
  fallback_latency_budget_ms: 30
```
jon: For admission control, my thought: check available capacity first, then check token-bucket. That way you only consume tokens if pool can serve within SLO.
aisha: We should gate change behind a rollout flag and synthetic traffic tests to avoid oscillations. Also add smoothing window for available_capacity (moving avg 30s).
maya: Agreed. Next steps: a) prototype refill formula in simulator b) add metrics & exports c) gate on feature flag + gradual rollout to eu-west-2.
nikhil: I'll own the simulator and metrics. @maya can you draft the feature flag rollout plan?
maya: Yep — will post a short RFC in #eng-platform this afternoon. :thumbsup:
jon: One more: billing impact. If we throttle more aggressively, spike in errors could lower usage-based revenue but reduce infra spend. We should model cost delta in RFC.
aisha: Noted. I'll pull cost curves for long-context jobs by model family.
maya: Cool. Let’s sync in the weekly infra sync with a short demo of the simulator.
nikhil: thanks all.
